stories.headline: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.title: US teen held over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship
stories.summary: New York, Oct 15 : A teenager was arrested for allegedly plotting to carry out a "mass shooting" at a Hindu place of worship in the US state of Illinois, with investigators recovering a manifesto expressing white supremacist ideology and references to violence against people of Indian descent. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, of Palatine village was arrested on October 11 and charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a weapon. According to investigators, the youth had tried to open fire "potentially targeting" the place of worship in the Aurora city in Illinois, but his gun jammed, forcing him to drive back home, a move that prevented a mass murder. The specific intended location has not been disclosed by the authorities. Palatine Police detectives examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)", which contained "statements expressing white supremacist and extremist ideologies, including references to violence directed toward individuals of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent". Detectives believe Paporakis may have been planning to carry out the attack on October 11. "However, the specific intended location has not been confirmed and remains under investigation," police said on Wednesday. The Consulate General of India in Chicago said it appreciated the timely action by law enforcement authorities and was in touch with members of the Indian diaspora while closely monitoring developments. The arrest comes amid celebrations of Hindu festivals, including Navaratri and Durga Puja, and just two weeks after the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights, Ohio, was vandalised. On October 11, the Palatine Police Department was contacted by the Mount Prospect Police Department regarding information it had received about a potential mass shooting. The information originated from an individual who reported receiving concerning electronic communications from Paporakis. According to a report by NBC Chicago, Paporakis had worked as a cashier at fast-food restaurant Taco Bell and had plotted to carry out a "mass shooting of Indian people" at a Hindu temple in Aurora. He drove to the temple last Sunday "decked out for war". The day he chose to carry out the carnage at the sprawling place of worship was filled with people. He was "one malfunctioning rifle away from becoming a mass shooter". Paporakis showed up "to kill a significant number of Indians", the report said, quoting police. Investigators said he had a "modified AR-style rifle and 300 rounds of ammo, enough to fill ten magazines for reloading, along with body armour, gasoline cans" and an assortment of Hakenkreuz (hooked cross used by Nazis), the report said. Paporakis allegedly drove from his mother's home in Palatine to the Aurora temple. Authorities said that "he tried to open fire but the gun jammed, so he drove home". There he "searched the internet trying to learn how to unjam his gun and called a colleague, informing them of (his) intent to carry out a mass shooting". The co-worker then notified the police, informing them of the plot, and Paporakis was arrested Sunday before he could return to the temple. The youth was arrested as he was leaving his residence following a coordinated response by the Palatine and Mount Prospect police departments. Paporakis has been charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of weapons. He appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday at the Cook County Third Municipal District Courthouse in Rolling Meadows, where a judge ordered him detained. His next court appearance is scheduled for October 30. According to investigators, Paporakis "expressed pleasure calling himself a sociopathic white supremacist Neo-Nazi filled with hatred, fantasising about mass murder nearly every day". In a social media post, the Hindu American Foundation commended law enforcement for swift action. "We also urge the community to stay vigilant and report any potential threat. Every community deserves to worship without fear," it said. The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) said the "disturbing plot" comes as Hindus gather in large numbers to celebrate Navratri, and just two weeks after an attack on a temple in Ohio. "Hindu temples and all houses of worship must be sanctuaries of peace, prayer, and solace - NEVER targets of hate, violence, or terror. We thank law enforcement for their swift action in averting what could have been an unspeakable tragedy. "We urge elected officials and law enforcement agencies to take the growing threats against Hindu places of worship seriously, strengthen protections, and unequivocally condemn Hinduphobia," it said in a social media post. The group called on temples and community organisations to review their security measures, remain vigilant, and promptly report suspicious activity. "The freedom to worship without fear is a fundamental American right. It must be protected," it said. Police said they were working with the FBI as the investigation continued, including a review of possible additional charges. Authorities have not identified any known ongoing threat to the public associated with the incident. "The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated... Protecting our communities and places of worship remains a priority," Palatine Police Chief William Nord said. FBI Chicago Special Agent in Charge Ryan Whalen said the agency aggressively works alongside its local and state law enforcement partners to identify, investigate, and dismantle any threats of violence driven by radical ideologies. PTI

stories.title: IDBI Bank shares fall 7% as investors book profit after Fairfax deal gets cabinet nod
stories.summary: Shares of IDBI Bank fell over 7% to Rs 83.87 on Thursday, a day after surging nearly 13% following the Union Cabinet’s approval of Fairfax’s acquisition of a 60.72% stake in the lender. The decline comes amid profit-booking after the stock’s sharp rally on the long-awaited privatisation development.The stock had climbed to Rs 93.60 on Wednesday, its highest level in nearly two weeks, taking IDBI Bank’s market capitalisation above Rs 1 lakh crore. The rally followed the Cabinet’s approval of the sale of the government’s and LIC’s combined stake to Fairfax Financial Holdings’ subsidiary, M/s 10955230 Canada Inc., for Rs 52,878.08 crore.Also Read |Redington could gain as memory shortage reshapes ICT distribution; brokerage sees 20% upsideFairfax deal closes a long chapter for IDBI BankThe deal marks a major step in the lender’s transformation after years of financial stress. Fairfax’s bid of Rs 81 per share was above the Rs 75.99 average fair valuation arrived at by two independent professional valuation agencies.The government will retain a 15% stake in IDBI Bank, while LIC will hold 19% after the transaction. The successful bidder will also have to go through the RBI’s ‘fit & proper’ assessment and secure other regulatory approvals before the deal is completed.The transaction is expected to become the largest foreign direct investment in India’s financial sector, according to Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. It also puts IDBI Bank at the centre of the government’s broader push to bring private and foreign capital into the banking sector.Also Read |Jio IPO fever grips telecom stocks: Airtel, Vodafone Idea & others rise up to 4%IDBI’s turnaround storyIDBI Bank today looks very different from the lender that once needed repeated government support. Its gross NPA ratio has fallen from 31.78% in September 2018 to 2.32% in March 2026, while net NPAs have dropped from 17.30% to 0.15%.The improvement has also shown up in profitability and growth. IDBI Bank reported a net profit of Rs 9,513 crore in FY26, while its total business rose 18% year-on-year to Rs 6.27 lakh crore as of September 30. Its latest quarterly business update showed deposits rising 17% to Rs 3.56 lakh crore and net advances growing 18% to Rs 2.72 lakh crore.With the privatisation now moving ahead, the next phase will be about what Fairfax does with the bank. The challenge will be to take a lender that has repaired its balance sheet and make it more competitive in the private banking space. stories.title: Rajasthan Awards Single Largest Solar-Plus-BESS Tender 2.45 GW at Rs. 3.42–3.53/kWh
stories.summary: After around nine months of issuing one of its largest solar-plus-battery energy storage system (BESS) tenders, Rajasthan Solar Park Development Company Limited (RSDCL) has awarded 2,450 MW of solar capacity paired with 1,600 MW/6,400 MWh of energy storage systems (ESS) at tariffs of Rs. 3.42–3.54/kWh. 30+ bidders participated in the Lot 2 of the RSDCL's solar plus bess tender, but only three bidders won this project around nine months after the tender was issued in January this year. The original tender covered up to 2,450 MW of solar capacity, divided into two lots. Lot 1 comprised 2,000 MW of solar capacity paired with 1,320 MW/5,280 MWh of BESS. The Lot 2 covered 450 MW of solar capacity paired with 280 MW/1,120 MWh of BESS, to be developed across two plots of 225 MW each. Rajasthan Awards Lot-1 Solar + BESS Tender Rs. 3.42/unit Under the Lot 1, two bidders secured solar plus BSS project in Rajasthan , Coal India Limitted (CIL) which won 225 MW solar plus storage project at Rs. 2.42/Unit and Actis backed India's renewable energy platform in India, Leo Energies won 225 MW tender at a tarrif of Rs. 3.43/unit each. Some other major bidders which bid for this project but didn't make it to the final bids were, KPI Green, NLC India, SAEL Industries, Engie, Ayana Renewables, Hinduja, Mahindra Susten among others. Rajasthan's 450 MW Solar + 280 MW/1,120 MWh BESS Tender Finds Three Bidders Under the RSDCL Lot 2, t hree bidders emerged as winners: NLC India Renewable Energy (NIRL), the renewable energy arm of NLC India; Rama Reflection India Pvt. Ltd.; and Coal India Ltd. NLC India secured a 1,000 MW solar-plus-BESS project at Pugal Solar Park, securing the largest individual project allocation at Rs. 3.53/unit. Rama Reflection won a 250 MW solar project 660 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS). Coal India also won a 1,000 MW solar-plus-BESS project at a slightly higher tariff of Rs. 3.54/unit. stories.headline: India To Add Record 70 GW+ Power Capacity In FY27, Minister Calls For AI-Led Solutions
stories.title: India To Add Record 70 GW+ Power Capacity In FY27, Minister Calls For AI-Led Solutions
stories.summary: India is likely to add more than 70 GW of power generation capacity in 2026-27, the highest addition in a single year, said Union Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs Manohar Lal. Sharing these estimages at an inaugural session of the Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) two-day international conference-cum-exhibition on, “Making Indian Power Sector AI-Enabled”, held virtually, Manohar Lal spoke about the need to make India’s power sector more intelligent. The event was held at the Manekshaw Centre in New Delhi. At the event, Manohar Lal emphasised that building a large and complex power system in the future would require not only producing more electricity but also managing it intelligently. He added that India’s installed power generation capacity had reached about 555 GW and that the country now needed to build a system capable of anticipating electricity demand. He also stressed the importance of better integrating renewable energy and energy storage, while ensuring an uninterrupted and affordable power supply for consumers. Lal called AI both a resource and a solution. According to him, AI can help forecast generation more accurately, improve grid management, plan maintenance in advance and detect power outages early. He said the sector must move from a reactive system to a predictive and proactive one, with attention to power data security and the responsible use of AI. Background The conference was being held on CEA’s 53rd Foundation Day. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, who also addressed the event virtually, said India had over 305 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity, accounting for close to 55% of its total installed capacity of 554.5 GW. He said the key question was how intelligently India could integrate, transmit, dispatch and consume clean energy. AI, he added, could improve renewable energy forecasting, support real-time grid balancing, optimise storage, reduce curtailment and help identify congestion in the network. “AI can help us convert data into intelligence, intelligence into timely decisions and decisions into better outcomes,” he said. He added that human oversight and accountability must remain central to critical grid operations and that India should develop AI solutions suited to Indian conditions and extend them to other emerging economies. September 2026: India Crosses 308 GW of Non-Fossil Capacity Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy Shripad Yesso Naik said India had reached 50% non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, more than five years ahead of its 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) timeline. As of September 30, 2026, non-fossil capacity had crossed 308 GW, including over 171 GW of solar and 59 GW of wind capacity. Peak power demand reached 256 GW in April 2026 and 270 GW in July 2026. He said India was no longer just building a bigger power system but a more complex one, and AI could help manage it. “Technology becomes meaningful only when it improves the life of our people,” he said, adding that AI must be reliable, explainable and secure. Minister of State for Commerce & Industry and Electronics & IT Jitin Prasada said the growth of AI, semiconductors and data centres depended on a corresponding expansion in power supply, particularly green power. He said India should make power as easy to access for AI as UPI had made digital payments. He added that the government was developing a policy for data centres and wanted to attract hyperscale investments without increasing electricity costs for consumers. He also spoke about skilling young people and avoiding supply chain bottlenecks in power equipment and semiconductor chips. Using AI to Build Grid Integration Capabilities Secretary, Ministry of Power, Pankaj Agarwal, said AI applications in the grid would require real-time action, with response times measured in milliseconds or less. He said India could offer renewable-rich regions for data centres. He urged the sector to scale up pilot projects into sustainable business cases. He added that a data governance committee would include industry representatives alongside government offices. Additional Secretary, MNRE, Shri Mayank Tiwari, said energy security was a core part of national security and that India needed to balance the growth of green and conventional energy sources. He welcomed the conference’s ten focused tracks, designed to produce actionable outcomes, and highlighted CEA’s in-house team of 54 engineers working across ten areas of AI. CEA Emphasises AI Use in Power Infrastructure CEA Chairperson Ghanshyam Prasad said the sector’s challenge had shifted from keeping the lights on to managing where power came from, where it flowed and when it was needed. He traced India’s journey from 13 GW of installed capacity at Independence to the development of a single national grid. He said the sector’s plans, standards and regulations were the runway, while AI was the aircraft that needed it. He added that CEA had established a dedicated team of 54 officers working on AI and that the sector needed to develop AI capabilities within its institutions rather than merely purchase solutions. During the session, CEA launched three documents and tools. Vidyut Dwar is an online portal for cross-border electricity trade, for which CEA is the designated authority responsible for approving electricity imports and exports with neighbouring countries. The portal brings the entire application process onto one platform, allowing applicants to submit documents online, track application status and access approvals. It is designed to make the process paperless, faster and more transparent. The dignitaries also unveiled the CEA Manual on Transmission Planning Criteria 2026, which covers capacity expansion, reliability, renewable energy integration, new technologies and the better utilisation of transmission corridors. It also includes planning criteria addressing right-of-way challenges. The third launch was the Unified Framework for Digitalisation of the Distribution Sector, which provides power distribution companies with a common direction for adopting digital technologies in a phased, need-based and outcome-oriented manner. The Central Electricity Authority is the technical and planning body of the Ministry of Power, Government of India. It advises on power sector planning, technical standards and safety.

He also stressed the importance of better integrating renewable energy and energy storage, while ensuring an uninterrupted and affordable power supply for consumers.
Lal called AI both a resource and a solution.
According to him, AI can help forecast generation more accurately, improve grid management, plan maintenance in advance and detect power outages early.
He said the sector must move from a reactive system to a predictive and proactive one, with attention to power data security and the responsible use of AI.
Background.
The conference was being held on CEA’s 53rd Foundation Day.
Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, who also addressed the event virtually, said India had over 305 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity, accounting for close to 55% of its total installed capacity of 554.5 GW.
He said the key question was how intelligently India could integrate, transmit, dispatch and consume clean energy.
AI, he added, could improve renewable energy forecasting, support real-time grid balancing, optimise storage, reduce curtailment and help identify congestion in the network.
“AI can help us convert data into intelligence, intelligence into timely decisions and decisions into better outcomes,” he said.

He added that human oversight and accountability must remain central to critical grid operations and that India should develop AI solutions suited to Indian conditions and extend them to other emerging economies.

He said India was no longer just building a bigger power system but a more complex one, and AI could help manage it.
“Technology becomes meaningful only when it improves the life of our people,” he said, adding that AI must be reliable, explainable and secure.

He said India should make power as easy to access for AI as UPI had made digital payments.
He added that the government was developing a policy for data centres and wanted to attract hyperscale investments without increasing electricity costs for consumers.
He also spoke about skilling young people and avoiding supply chain bottlenecks in power equipment and semiconductor chips.

He said India could offer renewable-rich regions for data centres.
He urged the sector to scale up pilot projects into sustainable business cases.
He added that a data governance committee would include industry representatives alongside government offices.
Additional Secretary, MNRE, Shri Mayank Tiwari, said energy security was a core part of national security and that India needed to balance the growth of green and conventional energy sources.
He welcomed the conference’s ten focused tracks, designed to produce actionable outcomes, and highlighted CEA’s in-house team of 54 engineers working across ten areas of AI.

Vidyut Dwar is an online portal for cross-border electricity trade, for which CEA is the designated authority responsible for approving electricity imports and exports with neighbouring countries.
The portal brings the entire application process onto one platform, allowing applicants to submit documents online, track application status and access approvals.
It is designed to make the process paperless, faster and more transparent.

The dignitaries also unveiled the CEA Manual on Transmission Planning Criteria 2026, which covers capacity expansion, reliability, renewable energy integration, new technologies and the better utilisation of transmission corridors.
It also includes planning criteria addressing right-of-way challenges.

The third launch was the Unified Framework for Digitalisation of the Distribution Sector, which provides power distribution companies with a common direction for adopting digital technologies in a phased, need-based and outcome-oriented manner.
The Central Electricity Authority is the technical and planning body of the Ministry of Power, Government of India.
It advises on power sector planning, technical standards and safety.

stories.headline: "Sonamarg to be developed as year-round tourism destination": CM Omar Abdullah
stories.title: "Sonamarg to be developed as year-round tourism destination": CM Omar Abdullah
stories.summary: Ganderbal, Oct 15 : Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Thursday said the Jammu and Kashmir government is working on projects to develop Sonamarg as a year-round tourism destination, with plans to promote rafting in summer and skiing, skating and other winter sports during the colder months. “With the construction of the tunnel, Sonamarg is now accessible throughout the year. We want to promote rafting during summer and skiing, skating and other winter sports activities,” Omar told reporters during his visit to Ganderbal, as per the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO). He said he would work with Kangan MLA Mian Mehar Ali to further strengthen Sonamarg’s position on the tourism map. The Chief Minister said forest, environmental and wildlife clearances sometimes caused delays in tourism projects, but maintained that the government would follow all required procedures while developing new tourism destinations. During his visit, he said development projects worth around Rs 60 crore were either inaugurated or had their foundation stones laid in Ganderbal. On the construction of a major bridge over the River Jhelum, estimated to cost Rs 40 crore, he said test piling had been completed and efforts were underway to meet the construction targets. “We are making efforts to complete the pillars by April and the entire bridge by December next year,” he said. The Chief Minister said several road projects, a new school building and infrastructure works at the Fruit and Vegetable Mandi were also inaugurated. He said traders at the mandi had sought its expansion, construction of a boundary wall and a grade separator. The matter, he said, had been discussed with National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) officials, while other demands had also been noted for necessary action. On the demand for fencing the Power Development Corporation (PDC) canal following repeated incidents involving loss of human lives, Omar said the matter would be taken up with the concerned authorities. “If the decision were within my authority, I would have announced it here. We will raise the public demand with the concerned authorities,” he said. Regarding pending compensation cases related to National Highway projects, Omar said newly appointed Deputy Commissioner Shreya would examine the matter after settling into her responsibilities. On traffic congestion caused by Chinar trees along the Beehama–Kheer Bhawani road, the Chief Minister acknowledged the difficulties faced by commuters and stressed the need for a practical solution. “Development and environmental protection must go hand in hand. We may have to remove some trees and plant eight to ten Chinar trees elsewhere, away from roads,” he said. Referring to the 70th National School Sports event being held at the College of Physical Education in Ganderbal, Omar said students from across the country were participating in Wushu and Taekwondo competitions. Reiterating his stand on land acquisition, the Chief Minister said written agreements signed with affected families would be honoured. “Whatever commitments were made in the signed agreements will be implemented,” he said.—(KNO)

stories.headline: Delhi protests: Union home secretary tenders unconditional apology to SC in contempt case
stories.title: Delhi protests: Union home secretary tenders unconditional apology to SC in contempt case
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan has tendered an unconditional and unqualified apology to the Supreme Court in a contempt case over alleged violation of the apex court's direction to ensure no “complete prohibition” on Metro and train services in Delhi in the wake of the October 10 protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party. In an affidavit filed in the top court, Mohan said a request was received from Delhi Police to suspend cellular internet services for one day, until 10 pm on October 10. “The request was duly processed and considered in accordance with law and was found to be a proportionate measure, having regard to the magnitude of the situation and the need to prevent any disturbance of public order in the national capital,” Mohan said. The home secretary said that cellular internet services were suspended from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10 within a radius of 4 km of Raisina Hill. He clarified that the suspension was confined to cellular internet services, and did not extend to non-cellular internet services or telecommunication services such as Wi-Fi or broadband. “I state and submit that the suspension of internet services for a limited period and within a defined geographical area, subject to the applicable statutory safeguards, is a recognised measure that may be considered for maintaining public order in appropriate circumstances,” he said. “I therefore respectfully pray that this court may be pleased to modify its order dated October 11 to the extent necessary to permit the suspension of internet services in situations of necessity, strictly in accordance with law and subject to the applicable statutory requirements and safeguards,” he said. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi is scheduled to hear the matter on Thursday. On October 11, the apex court said that contempt petitioners, who have alleged violations of the court's direction to ensure no complete prohibition on Metro and train services in Delhi due to the protest, have made out a “prima facie” case. The bench had issued notices to Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Chairperson D Thara. The CJP had given the protest call on October 10 to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities.
